label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 5 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; nobody answered within 10 minutes, which counts as denied, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

fault.name: money-unit
fault.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
fault.cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one
expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 08:11:58Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it sends each payment's amount to the provider in the wrong unit: we store amount_cents correctly, but the provider charges 100 times as much. For example, pmt_000230 is $12.91 in our records and was charged $1,291.00. Every payment from pmt_000230 on does this, which produces the payments_match_provider findings. The ledger books what the provider reports, so it stays balanced and matches the provider, while our payments table does not. pmt_000233 is pending on our side even though the provider charged it, possibly a request still in flight or one that failed after the charge. Still open: c4's trace does not record the amount we sent, and the deploy log does not show the setting's previous value.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider failed with 66 findings, each a provider charge of exactly 100x our amount_cents, starting at pmt_000230. The ledger is balanced and matches the provider, and refunds all match.
payments-api was redeployed at 08:11:58Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, the only deploy after the 08:10:26Z stack start.
pmt_000230, the first overcharged payment, was logged as succeeded at 08:11:59.397Z with amount_cents=1291, one second after the deploy.
pmt_000230's request went straight from payments-api to fake-provider POST /v1/payments and got a 200. No other service touches the charge amount, so payments-api's request sets it.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings before the 08:11:58Z deploy, so charges are sent in cents again. Then refund or correct the overcharged payments from pmt_000230 onward with the provider and fix the ledger entries that booked the inflated amounts. Check pmt_000233, which is pending here but charged at the provider.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or are retried for a short time. The rollback stops new overcharges but does not repair existing ones: about 66 customers were charged 100x, and the ledger holds the inflated amounts. Those need a separate refund and data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back payments-api misbehaves, redeploy the 08:11:58Z settings, but only after changing CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT to cents. Then rerun the money check to confirm new payments match the provider.
